restrictions: Two distinct 135-byte messages M(t) = U || 0^40 || U || 0^15, U the 40 little-endian bytes of a 320-bit parameter t, so that with SHA3 padding (byte 135 = 0x86) each message is one absorbed block. t ranges over the cosets t_j + span(W40), j < 256 G, of the 40-dimensional field W40 listed in proof.md Section 3, each origin t_j drawn from two fresh independent uniform random words (Section 6.1), in the Gray order of each coset.

Complete SHA3-256 sponge of sha3-256-r5-prefix-v1: zero initial state, rate 136 bytes, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 4 of Keccak-f[1600] in the single permutation call, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with reference operation cost 1355: a five-round call is one unit, every other operation 1/1355; generated straight-line code with immediate addresses, its generation charged in preprocessing (proof.md Section 5.1). With G = 1368445870808731089898285 groups, N = G Fv + G 4656 2^40 + S_v + 15 Q + 3554 R140 + (2^70 + 16) = 16278155856238756613402017182511090436254 word operations (Section 10); time_log2 = 123.1760 is log2(N/1355) rounded up, by the integer certificate 1355^10000 2^1231759 <= N^10000 < 1355^10000 2^1231760.

Memory below 2^141 words, 2^146 bytes: a direct sparse array of 2^140 words that is never initialized (the sparse-set table is correct for any initial memory, Lemma 8), dense key and identifier arrays of Q words each, coset records, work frames and generated code (Section 11.1). Preprocessing at most 2^70 + 16 word operations (below 2^59.60 target compressions), included in time_log2: code generation, constants, the certificate and the deterministic search that produced W40 (Section 11.2). No advice.

Success at least 0.39, a probability over the algorithm's coins (the random coset origins), rests on one declared heuristic, H_coset (proof.md Section 12): first- and second-moment rates of the candidates' digests (equal-digest pair rate at least, two-pair rates at most, the uniform values), which bound the existence of a collision by the Paley-Zygmund inequality (Lemma 10), and the mean and variance of the 140-bit false-match count and the bad-triple rate at most the uniform values. Proved in proof.md: two-round affinity on every coset of W40, degree at most 4 before the last chi, exactness of the Gray-order finite differences and of their initialization, the sparse-set table for arbitrary initial memory, the duplicate-coset bound, the second-moment identity, detection up to a bounded triple event, and every operation count.

No full-scale run and no collision are claimed. The two declared experiments execute the schedule at a reduced size (one group of 256 cosets with origins from the organizer's trial seeds, the first 2^9 Gray points of each, the full 140-bit key and table) through a counting machine that stops unless every executed count equals the formula of proof.md, and test a reduced-width form of H_coset on the run's own digests (proof.md Section 12.2): organizer-checked 16-bit mask events within one coset and across two cosets, and pair counts that must lie in stated intervals. A mask success is not a collision; nothing about cost is inferred.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. For the Q = 2^48 G candidates of CAMP (proof.md Sections 6.1 and 8: G = 1368445870808731089898285 groups of 256 cosets with independent uniform 320-bit origins, two random words each; inside each coset the 2^40 Gray points of span(W40) in the fixed order), with probabilities over the algorithm's coins: (a) the mean probability p2 that two candidates have equal 256-bit digests is at least 2^-256, and the mean probabilities p3 (two equal-digest pairs sharing one candidate) and p4 (two disjoint equal-digest pairs) are at most 2^-512; (b) the number Y of candidate pairs with equal 140-bit keys has E[Y] <= Q(Q - 1)/2^141 and Var[Y] <= Q(Q - 1)/2^141; (c) Pr[TRIPLE] <= Q(Q - 1)(Q - 2)/2^397, TRIPLE (a bad triple) as in proof.md Section 9. Independent uniform 256-bit digests meet every bound. Only first and second moments of pair counts and a first moment of triples are assumed, no occupancy or tail bound. With the exact identity E[X^2] = E[X] + 6 C(Q,3) p3 + 6 C(Q,4) p4 for the number X of equal-digest pairs and the Paley-Zygmund inequality (Lemma 10), (a) gives Pr[X >= 1] > 19993/51200 = 0.39 + 2/4096 by exact integer comparison at this G, the least such G; with Lemmas 7 to 9, (b) through Chebyshev's inequality for the verification cap R140, and (c), the success probability over the coins is greater than 0.39006709.
heuristics.scope: One enumeration of the actual campaign at full size: C = 256 G cosets with independent uniform origins, complete 40-dimensional cosets in Gray order, the full 256-bit five-round digest and its 140-bit key projection. The premise constrains only the mean pair rate and the mean two-pair rates of the campaign, the key-match mean and variance and the triple rate; class rates inside one coset and across two cosets at least (pairs), resp. at most (two pairs), the uniform values imply (a). Nothing else in the claim is heuristic: two-round affinity, the degree bound, the exactness of the enumeration, the sparse-set table, the duplicate-coset bound, the second-moment identity and every operation count are proved in proof.md Sections 3 to 10.
heuristics.extrapolation: Evidence on the five-round target. (1) Organizer-executed at every run of the two declared experiments (hcoset-within16, hcoset-cross16; proof.md Sections 12.2 and 13): on 2^17 digests of 256 cosets whose origins come from the organizer's trial seeds, the pair counts inside one coset at 16 bits and across cosets at 16 and 24 bits must lie within 4 standard deviations of their exact uniform expectations (511, 130560, 510) or the run fails, and the organizer recomputes every returned 16-bit agreeing pair, inside one coset (512 points) and across two independent-origin cosets (256 x 256 points); the exact uniform success probabilities per trial are 0.864841510863844 and 0.632121969489614, with pass intervals [200, 243] and [131, 192] successes of 256. These test pair rates and the existence event of Lemma 10 at reduced width. (2) GPU, preregistered (protocol hashed before the runs; pass rule: every count at least expected - 4 sigma; no reruns; proof.md Appendix A): random-origin field run P5 with control P6, 2^30 digests in 1024 cosets of a random 20-dimensional subspace of span(W40), exact equal-pair counts of 32-bit within-coset and 44-bit global projections (P5: z = -0.78 and +0.49; P6: -1.18 and -1.18); context: four five-round runs at deterministic origins and 17 six-round runs, 13 at uniform origins, every count within 2.1 sigma. (3) Sensitivity (proof.md Section 12.3): if the pair rate is (1 - eps) of uniform, the bound holds with the larger G listed there, for eps below 0.3751. The extrapolation is from 16- to 44-bit projections, 2^17 to 2^30 messages and 9- to 20-dimensional sub-cosets to the 256-bit digest and its 140-bit key, Q messages and complete 40-dimensional cosets.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption: no proof is known, and image size or balance do not imply it (a balanced linear map can be injective on every translate of a campaign space). On each coset every digest bit has degree at most 8 in the 40 inner variables, a real structure. The organizer-executed test reaches 16 and 24 bits and 2^17 digests per run; the GPU evidence reaches 44-bit projections and 2^30 digests, with one direct five-round random-origin run and its control. No test measures the two-pair rates p3 and p4, the key-match variance or triples at full width. The time bound is computed at eps = 0; a pair-rate shortfall eps needs the larger G of proof.md Section 12.3.
